rationale: SYSTEMIC, HIGH SEVERITY: the lesson's core heuristic "a decimal with n zeros between the point and the 1" for 10⁻ⁿ is off by one throughout — correct count is (n−1) zeros, since the 1 itself occupies the nth place. Self-contradicting on its own worked example: c1 states 10⁻³=0.001 has "n zeros" (3) but 0.001 actually has 2 zeros before the 1. Recurs in i2 (fallbackFeedback claims 10⁻⁴=0.0001 has "four zeros" — actually 3 — plus a self-undermining "count carefully" aside; commonErrors[1] claims 10⁻³ has "3 zeros before the 1" — actually 2), k3 (explanationVariants[1] and successFeedback both claim 10⁻⁵=0.00001 has "five zeros" — actually 4), ch1 (explanationVariants[0], commonBuilds for 10⁻⁴/10⁻⁶, hints[2] all repeat the off-by-one count), r1's takeaway, and the remedial concept. Grading keys/answers themselves are all correct (0.0001, 0.01, 0.00001 etc.); only the taught zero-counting rule is wrong, risking miscounted digits if a student applies the memorized heuristic to a new problem. Figure esn-power-meaning depicts only positive powers (10³=1000 etc.), which are correctly described (n zeros for 10ⁿ, n positive, IS correct) and unaffected.
